notes.text: These UCR programmes provide substantive related business study, with different emphases on strategy, digital ventures or people and organisational change. They do not reproduce VU’s supply-chain sequence, advanced accounting choice or dedicated specialisation thesis. Optional independent research is separate, requires approval and is outside the displayed 24-course, 180-EC schedules; it does not replace the VU thesis. A curriculum comparison does not establish degree equivalence, professional qualification or automatic master’s admission.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Business Administration studies organisations through strategy, marketing, accounting, finance, people, law, logistics and information technology. The selected Strategy and Organisation route combines these foundations with research methods, a specialisation and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three substantive related programmes: broad business strategy and decisions; digital business and new ventures; and people, leadership and organisational change. Their business courses are supported by different analytical tools. Computational courses teach general methods rather than guaranteed business applications. Supply-chain depth, advanced accounting and the dedicated VU specialisation thesis remain important differences.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 60 EC in year one, 48 EC of required second-year study and two 6 EC restricted choices, then 30 EC of open academic choice, 6 EC ethics, 12 EC specialisation courses and a 12 EC individual thesis. Accounting II and Entrepreneurship are selected choices rather than requirements for every student. Noncredit research participation gates the integration-course credits. The entry language assessment and any required remediation are part of Academic Skills; personal and professional development also carries no extra credits. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 48 EC. Minor entry, level, overlap and approval rules apply. Thesis entry requires completion of years one and two, with strict methods requirements and separate course/supervisor registration.
